Velvet Scroll

Your ebooks, scrolling at your pace.

About

Free · No account · Works offline

An ebook reader that scrolls for you

Press play and the page glides up at a steady pace, with a reading guide that holds your place. Turn on read aloud, set the text just how you like it, and keep your books private on your own device.

Also as a browser extension, which can save web articles: Chrome · Firefox · Edge · More about Velvet Scroll

Mode

About · Extensions: Chrome · Firefox · Edge · Privacy · Licences · Terms · Refunds · Velvet Scroll Plus · Books stay in this browser on this device; nothing is uploaded. Opens EPUB, KEPUB, MOBI, AZW3, PDF, TXT, HTML, FB2 and CBZ comic files, including zipped ones, and Word (DOCX), LibreOffice (ODT) and Markdown documents. Drag them anywhere on the page to add them. DRM-protected and password-locked books, including Kindle store purchases, can't be opened.

      Scroll style

      Moves the text in fractions of a pixel so it glides instead of stepping. Turn it off if text looks slightly soft while it scrolls.

      Colours

      Read aloud

      Starts from the line on the reading guide and keeps the spoken words on it. While it’s reading, tap any sentence to read from there, use the ⏮ ⏭ buttons (or ← →) to skip a paragraph, or pick a chapter from Contents. Uses the voices installed on your device.

      Story modePlus

      Your pictures stay on this device. They’re never uploaded or synced. The veil is the page colour behind the text; Phone focus picks which part of the picture shows on a phone.

      More: magnifier, dictionary, translate, refresh rate, shortcuts
      Magnifier

      Turn it on with the magnifier button or the M key. Drag its rim to move it, or the dot on the rim to resize it.

      Dictionary

      Select a word (or double-click it), then choose Define. Modern meanings come from WordNet, and older ones from Webster’s 1913 dictionary, for the words in classic books. It works offline once it’s downloaded (about 14 MB, once).

      Translate Experimental

      Experimental. Translates English books as you read, on this device, with Mozilla’s open-source translator (the one in Firefox). Machine translation makes mistakes, especially with old-fashioned or poetic writing, names and dialogue, so treat it as a reading aid, not a faithful translation. Highlights and notes are paused while it’s on.

      Motion

      Auto measures your screen. Choose a rate yourself if motion still judders, for example on a monitor that changes its rate.

        Note

        Document details

        Accessibility

        These settings apply everywhere: the library, the reader and every window.

        High contrast

        Colour vision

        Red–green suits protanopia and deuteranopia (the most common kinds); blue–yellow suits tritanopia. The accent, reading guide, word highlight and progress bars switch to colours that stay distinct, and selected buttons and warnings get ✓ and ⚠ marks so nothing relies on colour alone.

        Size

        Makes the buttons, menus and labels bigger and easier to tap. The book's own text size is under Display.

        Reading

        Switches the page to Atkinson Hyperlegible, a typeface designed for low vision, and adds a little space between letters and words, which some readers with dyslexia find helpful. Turning it off puts your typeface back.

        Motion

        Keyboard

        Turn these off if they clash with your screen reader or speech software. Space, the arrow keys and Page Up / Page Down still work, and every shortcut also has a button. With a screen reader, Read aloud (the speaker button in the reader) reads the book to you and follows along on the page.

        Appearance

        Colours for the library and panels. The reading page has its own colours under Display in the reader.

        Changes the words in Velvet Scroll’s menus and windows. Your books stay in their own language.

        Theme
        Accent colour
        Background

        Pick a light colour and it's used in the light theme; pick a dark one and it's used in the dark theme. Velvet Scroll makes a matching shade for the other theme, and adjusts the text and accent so they stay easy to read.

        Save an article

        Paste the address of an article, story or blog post. Velvet Scroll keeps a clean, readable copy in your library, with its pictures where the site allows.

        On a page you’re reading, you can also save it with the Velvet Scroll button in the browser toolbar, or by right-clicking the page.

        Add from a web address

        Paste a link to an ebook or PDF: EPUB, PDF, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, TXT or CBZ. Links to a book’s page on Project Gutenberg or arXiv work too, as do shared Dropbox, Google Drive and GitHub links. DRM-protected books can’t be added.

        Many sites don’t let other websites download their files. If a link doesn’t work here, download the file in your browser and use Add books, or use the Velvet Scroll browser extension, which can download from any site you allow.

        Natural voices

        Natural voices use Piper, an open-source speech system, to read aloud in a more lifelike voice than many built-in voices. It runs entirely on your device: nothing you read is sent anywhere.

        Before you turn it on
        • Downloads: about 20 MB the first time (the pronunciation dictionary and the speech engine), plus about 63 MB for each voice you choose, from jsDelivr and Hugging Face. Use Wi-Fi if your data is limited. Your browser keeps them, so they aren’t downloaded again unless you remove them or clear this site’s data.
        • Uses your device’s processor. Speech is made as you listen. On most computers and recent phones it’s made faster than it’s spoken. Older phones may pause briefly between sentences and use more battery.
        • English only, with British and American voices. Use a device voice for other languages.
        • Word highlighting is estimated, so it can run slightly ahead or behind the voice.
        • Openly licensed. The voices were trained on public-domain recordings. Pronunciation uses eSpeak NG, which is free software under the GPL 3.0 licence. See Licences for details and source code.

        You can switch back to a device voice at any time under Display, and remove the downloads there.

        Licences

        Recognise text

        Before you start
        • Runs on your device. Velvet Scroll reads the page images itself with Tesseract, an open-source text recogniser. Nothing from your book is uploaded.
        • A one-time download of about 7 MB (English language data and the recognition engine) from jsDelivr. Your browser keeps it, so it isn’t downloaded again unless you clear this site’s data.
        • Takes a little while: a second or two per page on most computers, longer on phones. You can keep reading while it works and stop at any time. Finished pages are kept.
        • Works best on clear, printed English. Other languages in the Latin alphabet come out less accurately, handwriting isn’t recognised, and there may be some mistakes.
        • Openly licensed. Tesseract and Tesseract.js are free software under the Apache 2.0 licence. See Licences for details.

        The recognised text is saved in this browser with the book, so it’s ready next time. Removing the book removes it too.

        Licences

        Translate (experimental)

        Before you turn it on
        • An experimental feature. It may be slow, make mistakes or not work on some devices, and it may change or be removed.
        • Machine translation, not a translator. It’s good for getting the gist and for language practice, but it can get meaning, tone, names and idioms wrong, especially in older or literary books.
        • Runs on your device. Nothing from your book is sent anywhere: the translator runs in your browser with Mozilla’s open-source Firefox Translations engine and models.
        • A one-time download of about 30 MB from velvetscroll.net. Your browser keeps it, so it isn’t downloaded again unless you remove it or clear this site’s data.
        • English books only for now, into Spanish. More languages may follow.
        • For your own reading. Velvet Scroll shows the translation on screen as you read; it never saves or shares a translated copy.
        • Openly licensed. The engine and models are free software from Mozilla under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. See Licences for details.

        Licences

        Backup and restore

        Save a backup

        One file with your books, covers, reading positions, shelves and settings. Keep it on a USB drive or in your own cloud storage, then restore it in Velvet Scroll on another computer or browser.

        With a password, the backup is encrypted with AES-256 and can't be opened without it. A forgotten password can't be recovered.

        Restore a backup

        Adds the books from a backup to this library. For books you already have, the most recent reading position and details are kept.

        Google Drive sync

        Keep your reading places, shelves, book details, highlights, notes and settings in step on all your devices, through one small file in your own Google Drive. Velvet Scroll can only see the files it creates there. The books themselves aren’t uploaded: copy them to each device once with a backup.

        In your Google Drive sync but not in this library:

          Browser sync

          Uses your browser's own sync between computers where you're signed in to the browser with extension syncing turned on. The books themselves aren't synced: copy them once with a backup, and after that your place follows you.

          In your synced library but not on this computer:

            Sync code

            Copy your reading places, shelves, book details and settings to another browser or device, with no account. The code is encrypted with a passphrase you choose. Books themselves aren’t included: copy them once with a backup, then use a sync code whenever you switch devices.

            Use a sync code

            In the code but not in this library (add them with a backup or the original files):

              Keep the passphrase separate from the code: anyone with both can see your reading list. A code is a snapshot, so make a new one each time you want to sync.
